site.title: Andrés Atencio — Software Developer · IT Teacher
site.description: Professional site of Andrés Atencio, Software Developer · IT Teacher.

paragraphs: Software development and IT teaching are one present trajectory. This page introduces the work, what can be inspected, and how to start a conversation.

experience.heading: Experience
paragraphs: Selected work, a reverse chronology of software roles, and current teaching sit in one chapter. Teaching belongs to the same practice; it does not replace development.

groups.heading: Selected work
paragraphs: A contained piece of work the reader can look at closely — the role, the period and what was actually done. Tools stay attached to that work.

groups.heading: Software chronology
paragraphs: Roles and periods in reverse order. Historical technologies remain with the jobs they belonged to, not in a separate skills list.

groups.heading: Teaching and practice
paragraphs: Current IT teaching and present technical practice, written in context and without inflated claims.

background.heading: Background
paragraphs: Completed qualification, pedagogical training and broader study. Incomplete paths stay incomplete; they are not treated as degrees.

groups.heading: Completed qualification
paragraphs: The finished academic credential that supports the public profile.

groups.heading: Pedagogical training
paragraphs: Preparation for teaching, kept distinct from a completed degree.

groups.heading: Broader study
paragraphs: Other multidisciplinary study, present as study rather than as an extra qualification.

workingTogether.heading: Working together
paragraphs: Suitable collaboration is described by the shape of the work, not by a sales pitch. A small, well-defined piece of work on an existing system is a natural way in.
Public availability stays generic: part-time and remote-friendly, without a weekly capacity.

contact.heading: Contact
paragraphs: A direct way to write, public profiles and the Software Development CV belong here. The CV is a utility reached from this page, not a chapter to scroll through.
